newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power boosted by cold, Gulf outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power boosted by cold, Gulf outages.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were sharply higher Monday as a Gulf cold front stretched into the region and the Gulf Coast area experienced power outages due to ice storms.
"Prices are way up, but I think there's still more room to the upside, considering these freezing temperatures," one trader said, noting the cold temperatures will likely remain through this week.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be about five to 15 degrees below-normal through midweek, but another cold front is forecast to pressure temperatures late this week or early next week.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday soared into the $34.50-35.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, as compared with Friday's range of $24.00-25.50.
Early peak deals into TVA were reported done as low as $23.00 per MWh, but prices quickly rose from this level.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices in northern TVA for Tuesday were assessed $2-3 higher around $17.00.

Firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks at the Georgia/Florida border for Tuesday delivery were also up about $10 to the $35.00-36.00 range, though some early deals were done as low as $28.00.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally higher at $18.00-19.00. In Alabama, firm, off-peak power sold in the $32.00-34.00 range, sources said.
In Florida, where below-normal temperatures are expected to remain about six to 12 degrees below-normal, firm, peak prices were talked in the $28.25-34.00 range.

The cold in Florida failed to spread as far south as forecasters had previously expected, thereby keeping some utilities out of the market. Most freezing temperatures were only felt in the panhandle, sources said.

As the cold, stormy weather knocked out power lines in Texas and kept furnaces and space heaters cranking, natural gas prices along the Gulf Coast rose an average of 10 cents to the $3.90-4.00 per million British thermal units range, which is about even with January indices.
